declared_purpose: A local-first market research toolkit providing Yahoo Finance quotes, fundamentals, trends, indicator charts and a combined summary/PNG report, with optional news search and options/flow research. These outputs are explicit promises; lookup breadth, repeated lookups and intermediate retention are implementation choices. Browser-first options access is recommended, while automated scraping is best-effort (SKILL.md:1-23, 70-78, 99-123).

data_operations.operation: Look up and retain ticker metadata
data_operations.data_scope: The complete returned metadata object, including quote, company identity and fundamental fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: yfinance, intended to access Yahoo Finance; returned metadata remains in the yf.py process. Exact remote endpoints are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Every non-option command, including history, pro and chart, performs this lookup before dispatch.

data_operations.source: Ticker object and command-line period, defaulting to 3mo in the CLI
data_operations.data_scope: Historical series; Close is used for ASCII/simple charts, while pro charts use price and volume data.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: yfinance history interface and local DataFrames; network versus cache servicing is unresolved.
data_operations.condition: history, pro, chart and report paths. Both report and pro invoke history again through another processing step.

data_operations.operation: Compute market indicators and return summaries
data_operations.data_scope: Price changes, fundamentals, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, VWAP, ATR and market labels such as Overbought or Bullish. These describe market data, not personal attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and terminal output to the caller.
data_operations.condition: According to the selected command and indicator flags; report automatically calculates its main indicators.

data_operations.operation: Persist chart images and return their paths
data_operations.source: Selected ticker, historical data and calculated indicators
data_operations.data_scope: PNG charts; pro charts include the ticker and period in their title. Filenames contain the ticker.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local /tmp/{symbol}_pro.png for pro/report and /tmp/{symbol}_simple.png for chart; paths are printed to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Pro/report save a chart when history is nonempty; chart uses its separate simple-chart implementation. Saving an image is an explicit required output. No cleanup is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Forward an augmented news query to a local helper
data_operations.source: news.py command-line query and search settings
data_operations.data_scope: Original query plus 'latest news earnings guidance', result limit, region and time limit; defaults include us-en and one week.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local ddg_search.py child process through command-line arguments; its output returns through inherited standard output.

data_operations.source: Direct helper query or augmented news.py query
data_operations.data_scope: Query, search kind, region, safesearch, time limit and result limit; text/news also receive backend selection. Optional proxy, timeout and TLS verification settings configure the client.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ddgs or fallback duckduckgo_search; actual search providers and any configured proxy are unresolved. The default backend is auto.
data_operations.condition: Only on optional search invocation. The helper supports text, news, images, videos and books; news.py selects news.

data_operations.data_scope: All returned records are materialized locally. JSON/JSONL emits complete records; Markdown emits titles, links and available body/snippet text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory and standard output to the caller; no file storage or onward disclosure is specified.
data_operations.condition: After the selected search completes; output format controls returned fields.

data_operations.data_scope: Ticker embedded in overview, live-flow and flow-history URLs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the caller. This helper performs no navigation.

data_operations.operation: Recommend optional browser navigation and visible-page summarization
data_operations.data_scope: Ticker in the requested URL; visible options/flow content for summarization.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Unusual Whales if a page is opened; a resulting summary may return to the caller. Browser and site behavior beyond this instruction is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Only if the optional browser-first workflow is followed; printing links does not trigger it.

data_operations.operation: Delegate the option command locally and return captured output
data_operations.data_scope: Symbol passed to uw.py; child stdout and stderr captured in memory. Stdout is printed, and stderr is printed on nonzero exit.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local python3 child process and the original caller.
data_operations.condition: The early option branch runs with a 25-second subprocess timeout and returns before any yfinance lookup. The later option branch is unreachable through this dispatch.

data_operations.operation: Navigate to Unusual Whales and extract options data
data_operations.source: Uppercased command-line ticker and rendered page content
data_operations.data_scope: Ticker-bearing overview URL; put/call ratio, volumes, premiums and sentiment. For JPM, INTC, IWM and XSP, also a live-flow URL and selected fields from at most the first 30 table rows.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Unusual Whales through headless Chromium with a fixed user-agent; extracted values remain in local dictionaries/lists.
data_operations.condition: Direct uw.py invocation or yf.py option. Overview navigation is attempted first; live flow requires an allowed ticker and successful preceding execution. The scraping finally block closes the browser.

data_operations.data_scope: Most frequent strike, bullish/bearish percentages, premium-threshold trade counts and volume-greater-than-open-interest flags; up to five qualifying trades are displayed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and console output to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Overview output depends on available data; flow insights require nonempty detailed flow. These are market/trade classifications, not established identities or personal holdings.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full ticker metadata lookup for history, pro and chart commands.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: yfinance lookup boundary and the yf.py metadata object; any resulting Yahoo Finance request is dependency-controlled.
potential_excess.condition: These commands execute the shared get_ticker_info call before using only ticker history.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Trend and chart generation require historical prices/volume; their implemented renderers do not use info.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Create a ticker object and retrieve the selected history.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Skip ticker.info for these paths. This removes a redundant lookup action rather than merely filtering its returned fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain history/error handling and the requested chart output. Whether this removes a network request depends on yfinance internals and caching.

potential_excess.data_scope: Metadata fields beyond those consumed by price, fundamentals and report.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The complete ticker.info object in yf.py memory; upstream response breadth is unresolved.
potential_excess.condition: A metadata-dependent command successfully obtains info.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These commands consume selected quote, identity, currency and fundamental fields, while the implementation obtains the entire returned object.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve the fields needed for the selected output, including existing price fallbacks.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a narrower upstream lookup if supported; otherwise retain only consumed fields locally. This concerns extra data in a necessary lookup.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep required fields, fallback behavior and symbol validation. Discarding fields after receipt reduces local retention only; availability of an upstream projection is unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated history lookup for the same ticker and period.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: yfinance history interface and additional local historical DataFrames.
potential_excess.condition: report fetches history before save_pro_chart fetches it again. pro fetches history in save_pro_chart and then again for a summary, even without RSI/BB summary flags.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A combined report/chart or chart/summary can use one historical dataset.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain sufficient history once for the requested chart and calculations.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Share the fetched DataFrame between rendering and summaries; omit summary processing when neither RSI nor BB is requested. This removes redundant calls, not required historical fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the requested period, indicators, empty-data behavior and outputs. Repeated calls are observable; repeated remote transfers are not established because caching is undocumented.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: DOM text copied into the local overview dictionary and returned to print_advanced_report.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The packaged report prints ratio, premiums and sentiment; it does not consume these volume fields.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Extract the overview fields used in the displayed report.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the two unused DOM reads and dictionary entries.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the printed overview and flow insights. This narrows local extraction only; the browser still loads the overview page.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw volume and oi values retained in each detailed-flow record after computing vol_gt_oi.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local detailed_flow list returned to print_advanced_report.
potential_excess.condition: A supported free-flow ticker yields a successfully parsed row.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Downstream reporting uses the comparison flag; it does not consume the retained raw volume or oi fields.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read and compare volume/open interest to calculate the unusual-entry flag.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep the raw values transiently for comparison, then retain only vol_gt_oi alongside fields needed for other insights.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the existing comparison and all printed insights. This reduces intermediate retention, not the necessary DOM reads or remote page load.

unknowns: Dependency implementations are absent. Exact yfinance endpoints, request payloads, cache behavior, ambient credential access, telemetry and persistence cannot be resolved; the source establishes API calls, not one remote transmission per call.
DDGS auto backend and fallback behavior leave the actual search-provider recipients unresolved. Proxy handling, provider retention and onward disclosure are not documented in the supplied source.
Browser subresource recipients, cookies, temporary files, site logging and server retention are unresolved. browser.close is resource cleanup, not evidence of data deletion.
PNG output is required, but file permissions, host retention and eventual deletion are unspecified. The packaged code provides no cleanup; /tmp placement alone does not establish expiry.
Caller handling of stdout, returned paths and summaries is outside the supplied source. No additional recipient or persistent conversation storage can be inferred.
These gaps block end-to-end recipient, retention and deletion conclusions; all supplied package files were assessed at source level.
